fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` and
`src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` both declare `trace_id` as
`["string","null"]`, described as "Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled; null otherwise",
but `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` passes a hardcoded `None` at every site that emits it. Nothing in
rebar produces a per-run identity, so a verdict cannot name the run that produced it and no
header can carry a run-stable value.

## Approach

Mint one identity per gate run at the two boundaries that already resolve the run's config
exactly once: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:167` (plan-review, `ctx.ticket_id` in
scope) and `:762` (completion-verifier, `ticket_id` in scope). Both open `gate_config(cfg)`,
whose contextvar every op reads back via `resolve_gate_config` (`config.py:99-107`). Attach it
with `dataclasses.replace(cfg, ...)` before `gate_config(cfg)`, so a caller-supplied config is
never mutated in place.

The identity carries exactly three values: `trace_id` (32 lowercase hex from
`secrets.token_hex(16)`), `ticket_id` (the boundary's own), and `operation` (the literal
`"plan_review"` or `"completion_verifier"`, per boundary). There is deliberately no `run_id`:
`trace_id` already identifies the run and a second identifier would have no consumer.
`ticket_id` and `operation` are minted here because the boundary is the only place they are
knowable; their consumer is the delivery ticket's `${run:...}` vocabulary
(`26ae-041f-dcc4-4279`, which depends on this one), and both are covered by criteria below so
they are verifiable in this change rather than resting on that follow-on.

The 32-hex lowercase shape matches the W3C trace-id format, so later work can supply a real
OpenTelemetry trace id into the same field with no schema or format migration. Random per run
rather than derived from the ticket id: a derived value would merge every re-review of a ticket
into one trace, and the verdict's own `trace_id` already provides the path back from a verdict
to its run.

The value reaches pool workers unchanged because both plan-review pools submit through
`generation._submit_ctx` — `ex.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, fn, *args)`
(`generation.py:154-165`), used by `pass1.py:426-427` and `container_stage.py:260`.

Populate the verdict by reading `req.config.trace_id` at **all three** `runner.py` sites that
currently hardcode `None`:

- `:254` — `FakeRunner.run`'s `mode == "structured"` branch, whose own comment reads "Structured
  mode (e.g. verify_completion)". The completion verifier is structured-mode, so a fake-runner
  completion verdict returns from here, not `:259`; omitting it would make the completion-path
  criterion below unsatisfiable against the fake runner.
- `:259` — `FakeRunner.run`'s findings branch.
- `:719` — the real runner.

The two `FakeRunner` branches are selected by `req.mode`, so testing one says nothing about the
other. The seam is `req.config`, not a runner attribute: the resolved gate config is handed to
the op as `RunRequest(config=...)` (`operations.py:209-212`), and `FakeRunner` holds no instance
config, already reaching configuration only through `req.config` (`req.config.repo_path` at
`:264`). Per-request derivations such as `max_output_cfg` build with `dataclasses.replace`, so
the identity rides through unchanged.

The emitted meaning of `trace_id` changes, so both schema files defining that vocabulary are
updated in the same change and the contract never contradicts the emitted value. The restated
wording is "per-gate-run correlation id (32 lowercase hex); null for deterministic or fallback
verdicts and standalone ops" — deliberately **not** "present inside any gate run". Other
emitters run inside a gate scope without any LLM call
(`workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:153`, `completion_reconcile.py:252`,
`workflow/completion_failures.py:98`), and `spec_scan.py:138` is not a gate op; all stay `None`
and are out of scope. A deterministic verdict has no gateway request behind it, so naming a
trace there would imply traffic that does not exist.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the identity fields on `LLMConfig`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — mint at both run boundaries.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — read `req.config.trace_id` at `:254`, `:259`, `:719`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `tests/unit/test_run_correlation.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests plus schema validation. The mechanism is contextvar propagation and
verdict field population, both of which run for real in-process; no subprocess or network
boundary is involved.

- Happy path: within one `gate_config` scope every `resolve_gate_config()` read returns the same
  `trace_id`, and a produced verdict carries it.
- Edge: two successive scopes differ; the value is `None` outside any gate run.
- Concurrency: a value read inside a `_submit_ctx`-submitted pool task equals the submitting
  thread's, exercising the real `copy_context()` seam rather than asserting on it structurally.
- Real-runner path: `:719` is driven through `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline
  `model_override` TestModel harness, so the real finalize path executes with no network call.
  Every other verdict assertion is satisfiable through `FakeRunner`, which would leave the
  `:719` edit unproven.
- Both gate surfaces: the plan-review and completion-verifier boundaries each produce a verdict
  carrying the run's `trace_id`, each validated against its own schema. Testing only the
  plan-review side would leave half the changed surface unverified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inside one gate run `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` is identical across repeated reads;
      checked by a test asserting equality across three reads in one scope.
- [ ] Two gate runs produce different `trace_id` values; checked by a test over two scopes.
- [ ] `trace_id` is 32 lowercase hex characters; checked by
      `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", value)`.
- [ ] A value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's; checked by
      a test submitting a reader through the real `_submit_ctx`.
- [ ] Within a gate scope `resolve_gate_config().ticket_id` and `.operation` equal what the
      boundary minted them from; checked by a test asserting both, for each boundary.
- [ ] A plan-review verdict carries the run's `trace_id` and validates against
      `review_result.schema.json`; checked by asserting the field and running the validator.
- [ ] A completion-verifier verdict produced in a completion-verifier scope carries that run's
      `trace_id` and validates against `completion_verdict.schema.json`; checked by asserting
      the field equals `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` and running the validator.
- [ ] Both schema files describe `trace_id` as a per-gate-run correlation id in W3C 32-hex
      shape, null for deterministic or fallback verdicts and standalone ops, with no residual
      Langfuse claim and no "present inside any gate run" wording; checked by a grep asserting
      "Langfuse" is absent and that the deterministic/fallback exemption is stated.
- [ ] A deterministic completion verdict produced inside a gate scope still carries
      `trace_id: null`; checked by a test driving the deterministic child-closure path and
      asserting the field, proving the contract matches the emitters left out of scope.
- [ ] The identity survives a per-request config derivation; checked by asserting
      `max_output_cfg(cfg).trace_id == cfg.trace_id`.
- [ ] A verdict produced through the real runner site `:719` carries `req.config.trace_id`;
      checked by a test driving `PydanticAIRunner.run` inside a gate scope with the offline
      `model_override` TestModel harness, so the assertion cannot be satisfied by a
      `FakeRunner` branch.
- [ ] Outside any gate run the identity is `None` and verdicts are unchanged; checked by a test
      asserting `trace_id is None` for a standalone op.
